story: The FCC lets GCI buy Quintillion's Arctic subsea fiber license, with price conditions, and names Starlink as the competitive check (DA 26-1124, October 20th)

claims.claim: The FCC approved, with conditions, the transfer of control of Quintillion's submarine cable landing license to GCI.
claims.verbatim: we approve with conditions, the application filed by GCI and Quintillion for approval to transfer control of a submarine cable landing license from Quintillion to GCI.
claims.notes: Para 1 of DA 26-1124. Issued 'By the Chief, Office of International Affairs', signed Thomas P. Sullivan. Para 1 also says 'on balance, the grant of the application, as conditioned, will serve the public interest.' Live FCC URL fetched and matched the local copy. Corroborated by Broadband Breakfast, October 26th, which names International Affairs Chief Thomas Sullivan.

claims.claim: The FCC released the order on October 20th.
claims.verbatim: Released: October 20, 2026
claims.notes: It was adopted the same day. Para 32 makes it effective on release.

claims.claim: The FCC denied the petition to deny filed by Alaska Communications (ACS).
claims.verbatim: we also deny the Petition to Deny filed by Alaska Communications Systems Holding, Inc. (ACS)
claims.notes: Para 1. The ordering clause, para 30, reads 'petition to deny the application is DENIED.' ACS filed the petition on July 16th (para 6).

claims.claim: The Quintillion System connects Prudhoe Bay, Barrow, Wainwright, Point Hope, Kotzebue and Nome.
claims.verbatim: a non-common carrier submarine cable system licensed in 2017, which connects several points within Alaska: Prudhoe Bay, Barrow, Wainwright, Point Hope, Kotzebue, and Nome.
claims.notes: Para 3. The system was licensed in 2017. Barrow is now Utqiagvik, the name the Appendix A list uses.

claims.claim: The Quintillion System is 1,176 miles long.
claims.verbatim: The Quintillion System is 1,176 miles in length and comprised of three fiber pairs and six cable landing station sites.
claims.notes: Para 3, citing Application at 4. Confirmed on the live FCC page.

claims.claim: The Quintillion System has three fiber pairs.
claims.verbatim: The Quintillion System is 1,176 miles in length and comprised of three fiber pairs and six cable landing station sites.
claims.notes: Para 3. The applicants say two pairs currently carry traffic on each segment and the third is 'reserved for future use.'

claims.claim: The Quintillion System has six cable landing station sites.
claims.verbatim: The Quintillion System is 1,176 miles in length and comprised of three fiber pairs and six cable landing station sites.
claims.notes: Para 3. This matches the six points named in C04.

claims.claim: Each Quintillion fiber pair has an initial design capacity of 10 Tbps.
claims.verbatim: Each fiber pair has an initial design capacity of 10 Tbps.
claims.notes: Para 3, from the application. This is design capacity, not lit or used capacity. Don't multiply it to 30 Tbps of usable capacity, because only two pairs are in use.

claims.claim: On April 1st the FCC granted a modification of Quintillion's license for the Nome to Homer Express extension.
claims.verbatim: On April 1, 2026, the Commission granted the modification of the cable landing license for the Quintillion Submarine Cable System
claims.notes: Para 3, citing DA 26-324, which is earlier background. The project is called the 'Nome to Homer Express,' or NTHE.

claims.claim: The NTHE extension runs from Nome to three new landing points at Emmonak, Hooper Bay and Naknek.
claims.verbatim: from the existing landing in Nome, Alaska to three new landing points: Emmonak, Hooper Bay, and Naknek, Alaska
claims.notes: Para 3. The extension is under construction, so it isn't operating yet.

claims.claim: GCI agreed to acquire Quintillion's parent at a $310 million enterprise value.
claims.verbatim: at a $310 million enterprise value, subject to working-capital and other adjustments.
claims.notes: Para 5. The securities purchase agreement was signed April 21st, which is background. Broadband Breakfast, October 26th, independently reports $310 million. The figure is subject to adjustments, so call it a $310 million enterprise value and not a price paid.

claims.claim: GCI will reimburse up to $50 million of qualifying capital spending on Quintillion's NTHE project.
claims.verbatim: GCI Holdings will reimburse up to $50 million of qualifying capital expenditures
claims.notes: Para 5, attributed to 'The Applicants state.' It's a ceiling, not a committed amount. Suggested phrasing: 'up to $50 million, according to the application.'

claims.claim: Additional earnout payments may be owed in 2028, 2029 and 2031 if certain financial metrics are met.
claims.verbatim: Additional consideration may be payable in 2028, 2029, and 2031 through a post-closing earnout dependent on achievement of certain financial metrics.
claims.notes: Para 5. These payments are contingent. Write 'may be payable', never 'will be paid.' No amount is disclosed.

claims.claim: Quintillion Subsea will continue to own all segments of the Quintillion System after the deal.
claims.verbatim: Quintillion Subsea will continue to own all segments of the Quintillion System.
claims.notes: Para 5, attributed to the applicants. Only the indirect ownership changes. GCI will hold 100% of Q Gateway Intermediate Holdings and so indirectly wholly own and control Quintillion Subsea. Suggested phrasing: 'the applicants say Quintillion Subsea keeps the cable itself.'

claims.claim: ACS argued that "GCI and Quintillion currently are the only providers of middle mile transport for substantial portions of Western and Northern Alaska, respectively."
claims.verbatim: GCI and Quintillion currently are the only providers of middle mile transport for substantial portions of Western and Northern Alaska, respectively.
claims.notes: Para 13 quotes ACS Petition to Deny at 7. On the page the quote sits inside curly quotation marks. The quote belongs to the company ACS, not to a named person.

claims.claim: ACS maintains that the Universal Service Fund will bear the cost of GCI monopoly pricing.
claims.verbatim: ACS maintains that the Universal Service Fund (USF) will bear the cost of GCI
claims.notes: Para 13, citing Singer Declaration at 31. The full sentence ends with a curly apostrophe followed by 's monopoly pricing.' This is ACS's allegation, which the FCC didn't adopt. Attribute it to ACS.

claims.claim: The FCC said competitive concerns are largely mitigated by lower marginal cost, the end of double marginalization and the growing presence of LEO satellite providers, particularly Starlink.
claims.verbatim: these are largely mitigated by several factors, including reductions in marginal cost, elimination of double marginalization, and the recent and growing competitive presence of Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite providers, particularly Starlink.
claims.notes: Para 12. Para 24 repeats it, calling Starlink and other LEOs 'importantly' a constraint. Broadband Breakfast, October 26th, corroborates the Starlink framing.

claims.claim: The FCC acknowledged disagreement in the record over whether Starlink is currently providing wholesale middle mile transport service in Alaska.
claims.verbatim: We acknowledge that there is disagreement in the record as to whether Starlink is currently providing wholesale middle mile transport service in Alaska.
claims.notes: Para 19, confirmed on the live page. The order contrasts the applicants' September 14th ex parte, which says Starlink Bonded Gateways provide middle mile connectivity, with ACS's September 22nd ex parte. ACS denied using a Starlink Bonded Gateway 'as a general replacement, or even as a backup, for middle mile services in Sitka.'

claims.claim: The FCC found nothing in the record to suggest that Starlink or another LEO provider could not provide wholesale middle mile service, regardless of whether Starlink provides it today.
claims.verbatim: regardless of whether Starlink is currently providing wholesale middle mile transport service in Alaska, we find nothing in the record to suggest that it or another LEO could not provide such wholesale service
claims.notes: Para 19. The sentence opens with 'Nevertheless,' and continues 'particularly if GCI were to attempt to raise the price of wholesale middle mile transport service post-merger.' This is a finding about potential, not a finding that Starlink provides wholesale middle mile service today. Keep it paired with C18.

claims.claim: Starlink began offering service in Alaska in November 2022, according to the FCC.
claims.verbatim: Since Starlink began offering service in Alaska in November 2022, it appears that thousands of residential customers have signed up for Starlink service.
claims.notes: Para 18. The 'thousands of residential customers' clause is hedged with 'it appears' and should stay hedged if used. The same paragraph says the Lower Yukon School District switched to lower cost satellite service, and that GCI claims rural health care facilities are beginning to take Starlink. That second point is GCI's claim and needs attribution.

claims.claim: During Quintillion's 2025 outage, GCI moved traffic to its microwave system and was forced to drastically limit speeds, according to the applicants.
claims.verbatim: GCI moved traffic to its microwave system and was forced to drastically limit speeds
claims.notes: Para 16. The FCC is quoting the applicants' September 14th ex parte at 3-4, so this is GCI's own account. Attribute it: 'GCI told the FCC it moved traffic to microwave.'

claims.claim: The applicants described Quintillion's 2025 outage as lasting seven-plus months.
claims.verbatim: seven-plus month outage in 2025
claims.notes: Para 16, in the applicants' words. The figures disagree. Broadband Breakfast, October 22nd, 2025 (background), calls it 'a near nine-month service disruption,' and the order cites that article in para 12 under the headline 'Restores Connectivity After 9 Months.' Both can be true because seven-plus is a floor. Don't print a single exact length. Suggested phrasing: 'an outage of seven to nine months, by differing accounts' or 'months-long.'

claims.claim: The applicants say the deal will enable an upgrade of the Quintillion-GCI network gateways to 100 Gbps from 10 Gbps.
claims.verbatim: the transaction will enable an upgrade of the Quintillion-GCI network gateways to 100 Gbps from the current level of 10 Gbps.
claims.notes: Para 25. It's an applicant claim that the FCC found 'creditable' in para 26. This is a projected benefit, so write 'expected to' or 'the companies say.' The applicants also claim the deal creates three new self-healing fiber rings.

claims.claim: As a condition, GCI must honor and extend any Quintillion contract in effect at closing for the life of the system, at the counterparty's choice.
claims.verbatim: at the sole discretion of the counterparty for the life of the system on which such services are purchased
claims.notes: Appendix A, commitment 1, the Wholesale Contract Commitment in the October 19th letter. Para 20 makes the commitments conditions of approval, and para 21 summarizes this one.

claims.claim: Existing Quintillion wholesale customers may order new services at their rural pricing to Nome to Homer Express locations once those are available.
claims.verbatim: to any and all locations on the Quintillion Rural Network, including those served by fiber networks under construction at the time of closing (e.g. Nome to Homer Express), once available
claims.notes: Appendix A, commitment 1. The pricing table applies to orders 'pursuant to that pricing table.'

claims.claim: GCI may adjust contract prices for inflation only if 12-month inflation exceeded 5 percent on the Anchorage consumer price index for all urban consumers.
claims.verbatim: inflation for the preceding 12 months exceeded 5% based on the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers
claims.notes: Appendix A, commitments 1 and 2. On the page the index name is followed by a dash and 'Anchorage'. The verbatim stops before the dash to respect the no-dash rule. The adjustment can't exceed the preceding 12-month inflation rate.

claims.claim: Any inflation adjustment can apply no earlier than three years after closing.
claims.verbatim: would apply no earlier than three years from closing
claims.notes: Appendix A, commitments 1 and 2. Para 21 summarizes it as 'for those years three years after closing.' Closing hasn't happened yet.

claims.claim: GCI may apply no more than one inflation adjustment per year.
claims.verbatim: GCI will not apply more than one inflation adjustment per year, and the adjustment will not exceed the inflation rate of the preceding 12-month period.
claims.notes: Appendix A, commitments 1 and 2.

claims.claim: GCI must give the FCC copies of covered contracts whose monthly recurring charge exceeds $5,000 per circuit.
claims.verbatim: where the monthly recurring charge is greater than $5,000 by circuit or $10,000 in the aggregate
claims.notes: Appendix A, commitment 4, the Contract Disclosure Commitment. It covers wholesale and enterprise contracts on the Quintillion Rural Network and in GCI Overlapping Communities.

claims.claim: The disclosure duty also covers contracts whose monthly recurring charge exceeds $10,000 in the aggregate.
claims.verbatim: where the monthly recurring charge is greater than $5,000 by circuit or $10,000 in the aggregate
claims.notes: Appendix A, commitment 4.

claims.claim: The contract disclosure duty lasts seven years after closing for wholesale contracts.
claims.verbatim: for seven (7) years following closing with respect to wholesale contracts and for five (5) years with respect to all other contracts.
claims.notes: Appendix A, commitment 4. Existing contracts are due within 60 days of closing, and new or revised ones every six months after that.

claims.claim: The contract disclosure duty lasts five years for all other contracts.
claims.verbatim: for seven (7) years following closing with respect to wholesale contracts and for five (5) years with respect to all other contracts.
claims.notes: Appendix A, commitment 4.

claims.claim: All contract documentation goes to the FCC under seal on a confidential basis.
claims.verbatim: All documentation will be provided under seal on a confidential basis.
claims.notes: Appendix A, commitment 4. Para 23 adds that the contracts may be used in any compliance proceeding. The public won't see the prices.

claims.claim: The Quintillion Rural Network is planned to have points of presence in 13 communities.
claims.verbatim: Utqiagvik, Wainwright, Point Hope, Kotzebue, Nome, Emmonak, Alakanuk, Nunam Iqua, Scammon Bay, Chevak, Hooper Bay, South Naknek, and Iguigig.
claims.notes: Appendix A, page 2. I counted 13 names. The list is introduced with 'Based on current construction plans', so write 'planned'. The page misspells Igiugig as 'Iguigig' here and spells it correctly in the Overlapping list. Use Igiugig in prose.

claims.claim: The order names 10 GCI Overlapping Communities, served or to be served by both GCI and Quintillion.
claims.verbatim: The GCI Overlapping Communities are Kotzebue, Nome, Emmonak, Alakanuk, Nunam Iqua, Scammon Bay, Chevak, Hooper Bay, Naknek/South Naknek, and Igiugig.
claims.notes: Appendix A, commitment 2. I counted 10 entries, with Naknek/South Naknek as one. Some overlap depends on grant-funded builds that aren't finished. Commitment 3 requires open access at just and reasonable rates.

claims.claim: Petitions for reconsideration of the order may be filed within thirty days of its release.
claims.verbatim: may be filed within thirty days of the release date of this Memorandum Opinion and Order.
claims.notes: Para 32. It applies to petitions under 47 CFR 1.106 and applications for review under 1.115. Thirty days from October 20th is November 19th. That date is my arithmetic and isn't printed in the order.

claims.claim: The text of the FCC order does not mention artificial intelligence or data centers.
claims.verbatim: MEMORANDUM OPINION AND ORDER
claims.notes: This is a negative claim, so no single string proves it. I read the full local copy, all 216 lines including Appendix A, and the WebFetch of the live FCC URL reported that 'artificial intelligence', 'data center' and 'AI' as a standalone word don't appear. The deck must not imply the order is about AI.

claims.claim: GCI called the FCC approval "an important step to completing the transaction," Broadband Breakfast reported.
claims.verbatim: This is an important step to completing the transaction.
claims.notes: In window. Written by Akshaya Krishnan. The page attributes the quote to a GCI statement and not to a named person. It shows the deal hasn't closed yet. The page also reports the $310 million figure.

claims.claim: Quintillion's cable near Oliktok Point was severed by sea ice in January 2025, Broadband Breakfast reported.
claims.verbatim: near Oliktok Point, which was severed by sea ice in January
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, from before the window, by Jericho Casper. The year comes from the October 2025 publication date and the 'near nine-month' duration. The page says the outage affected North Slope and Northwest Arctic Borough communities. The FCC order cites this article in para 12, and its 2025 outage reference agrees.

claims.claim: GCI said in June it would use Starlink's dedicated service with bonded gateways to strengthen network resiliency.
claims.verbatim: dedicated service with bonded gateways to strengthen its ability
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, released June 11th. The FCC order cites this release in para 19. It calls the service 'a valuable new layer of resiliency that complements our existing fiber, microwave, and satellite infrastructure.' It does NOT use the words 'middle mile' or 'backup', so don't say GCI uses Starlink for middle mile.

claims.claim: COMPUTE THREAD. The North Slope Borough is planning a natural gas power plant near Prudhoe Bay with private partners.
claims.verbatim: near Prudhoe Bay, which would generate electricity for industry, data centers and potentially a power line to the Railbelt.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, from before the window. The Alaska Current, October 3rd (also background), corroborates it: the project 'will tap into nearly 30 trillion cubic feet of proven natural gas reserves in Prudhoe Bay.' The plant is a plan and doesn't exist. Suggested phrasing: 'is planning' or 'proposes.' The two sources give different reserve figures, NSP's pitch saying 35 tcf and the Current about 30, so don't cite reserves. Nothing ties this to the FCC order.

claims.claim: COMPUTE THREAD. North Slope Power's proponents describe a 3 gigawatt first phase for the Prudhoe Bay gas plant.
claims.verbatim: The proponents said it would be a 3 gigawatt first phase that could be expanded to 10 gigawatts.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. 3 gigawatts equals 3,000 MW, so if the deck prints '3,000 MW' it must keep this claim id. The Alaska Current, October 3rd, corroborates it: the plant is 'developing a 3 gigawatt natural gas plant.' This is the proponents' projection, so write 'proponents say' or 'planned.'

claims.claim: COMPUTE THREAD. North Slope Power describes the plant as designed to power colocated AI data centers and industrial load.
claims.verbatim: Designed to power colocated AI data centers and industrial load
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. Cole is quoting North Slope Power's own CERAWeek pitch language. The Alaska Current, October 3rd, corroborates it: the project aims 'to deliver electricity to colocated AI data centers.' Attribute the purpose to North Slope Power.

claims.claim: COMPUTE THREAD. Proponents say the North Slope plant could later be expanded to 10 gigawatts.
claims.verbatim: The proponents said it would be a 3 gigawatt first phase that could be expanded to 10 gigawatts.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. This is an aspiration. The Alaska Current, October 3rd, corroborates it: 'with plans to scale to a world record-breaking 10 gigawatts.' Always hedge it with 'could' or 'proponents say.'

claims.claim: COMPUTE THREAD. The North Slope Borough and Twenty First Century Utilities partnered to create North Slope Power.
claims.verbatim: The North Slope Borough and Twenty First Century Utilities have partnered to create North Slope Power (NSP)
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The Alaska Current, October 3rd, corroborates it, calling Twenty First Century Utilities 'the borough's corporate partner in North Slope Power.'

claims.claim: COMPUTE THREAD. The Air Force announced in April that it would open military bases in Alaska to data center developers, The Alaska Current reported.
claims.verbatim: the Air Force announced in April that it would open military bases in Alaska to data center developers.
claims.notes: In window. The American Homefront Project via WHRO, September 28th, independently corroborates that the offer exists: 'The Pentagon has offered to lease about 4,700 acres of government land in the state to private companies,' with 'no projects have been awarded yet,' and sites considered 'in Anchorage, Healy, and Fairbanks.' Neither page ties the Alaska sites specifically to AI, so don't write 'AI data centers' here. I couldn't reach an Air Force primary document.

claims.claim: The Alaska Current reported that Peter Corsell contributed $14,000 in support of Sen. Dan Sullivan's reelection.
claims.verbatim: All told, Corsell contributed $14,000 in support of Sullivan
claims.notes: This claim is that the article SAYS $14,000, not that $14,000 is correct. The article's table lists May 1 as $7,000 to the candidate committee and $7,000 to Sullivan Victory. The article's network total is $58,000, from $29,000 plus $29,000, and the same double-count question applies to it. Written by Lauren Windsor.

claims.claim: FEC records show Peter Corsell gave $7,000 to the joint fundraising committee Sullivan Victory on May 1st.
claims.verbatim: CORSELL, PETER / SULLIVAN VICTORY (C00609255) / contribution_receipt_amount 7000.0 / contribution_receipt_date 2026-05-01 / receipt_type_full CONTRIBUTION
claims.notes: The source is a JSON API record, and the verbatim joins its field values with slashes. date_of_source is the receipt date, and the record was retrieved November 1st. This query covers all of Corsell's 2026-cycle Schedule A entries, and the only Sullivan-committee items are this one and the two memos in R03.

claims.claim: FEC records show the two $3,500 entries from Corsell to Alaskans for Dan Sullivan on May 1st are marked as transfer memos.
claims.verbatim: TRANSFER MEMO
claims.notes: Both entries are committee C00570994, amount 3500.0, memo_code X, memo_text 'TRANSFER MEMO'. Memo-coded items itemize how a joint fundraising transfer was allocated and aren't separate gifts. The two $3,500 entries add up to the same $7,000 in R02, which suggests the article's $14,000 counts it twice. That is an inference from FEC conventions. Suggested phrasing: 'FEC filings show $7,000, itemized again as transfer memos.'

claims.claim: FEC records list Corsell's employer on the Sullivan contributions as Twenty First Century Utilities.
claims.verbatim: TWENTY FIRST CENTURY UTILITIES
claims.notes: Occupation is listed as INVESTOR. Twenty First Century Utilities is North Slope Power's partner (C45), which links this runner-up to the compute thread.

claims.claim: FEC records show Charles Hu gave $7,000 to Sullivan Victory on April 24th, itemized as two $3,500 transfer memos to Alaskans for Dan Sullivan.
claims.verbatim: HU, CHARLES / SAIGE CONSULTING / SULLIVAN VICTORY (C00609255) / contribution_receipt_amount 7000.0 / contribution_receipt_date 2026-04-24
claims.notes: The source is a JSON API record. There are two C00570994 entries of 3500.0 each, memo_code X, 'TRANSFER MEMO', dated 2026-04-24. Hu is listed as managing partner at Saige Consulting. The article's table dates the gift April 26, but the FEC says April 24th, so use the FEC date. This query was filtered to the two Sullivan committees.

claims.claim: The Alaska Current reported that Saige managing partner Charles Hu donated $14,000 to Sullivan's candidate and joint fundraising committees.
claims.verbatim: Saige managing partner Charles Hu donated $14,000 to Sullivan
claims.notes: This claim is about what the article says. Compare R05, where the FEC record shows $7,000 plus memo itemizations.

stories_surviving: FCC grants GCI's acquisition of Quintillion's Arctic subsea cable license with price conditions and names Starlink as the competitive check (C01 to C40)
Compute thread, North Slope Power's planned Prudhoe Bay gas plant for colocated AI data centers and the Air Force opening Alaska bases to data center developers (C41 to C46)
Data center utility executives' gifts to Sen. Dan Sullivan, FEC record vs The Alaska Current's $14,000 figures (R01 to R06)

killed.claim: The Air Force is offering about 4,700 acres at Alaska bases for data centers.
killed.why: Only one secondary source supports it (American Homefront Project via WHRO, September 28th), and that page says 'the Pentagon', not the Air Force. No primary source could be reached because Bing and DuckDuckGo searches returned nothing relevant or a bot wall. The figure is kept in C46 notes as corroboration only and must not be printed.

killed.claim: The Air Force land offer includes Clear Space Force Station.
killed.why: No fetched page names Clear. WHRO names Anchorage, Healy and Fairbanks, and The Alaska Current names only Elmendorf.

killed.claim: The Air Force solicitation number is AFCEC-26-R-0006.
killed.why: It isn't on any fetched page, and searches for it returned only generic AFCEC pages.

killed.claim: The Air Force is offering Alaska base land specifically for AI data centers.
killed.why: WHRO links the military's AI push to data centers only nationally, and The Alaska Current says 'data center developers'. Neither ties the Alaska sites to AI.

killed.claim: Charles Hu's Sullivan gifts were made on April 26.
killed.why: The FEC record shows a receipt date of 2026-04-24. The article's table date is contradicted by the primary record.

killed.claim: GCI uses Starlink bonded gateways for middle mile or as a backup.
killed.why: The GCI June 11th release uses neither 'middle mile' nor 'backup' and calls the service a resiliency layer. The middle mile framing belongs to the applicants' FCC ex parte, and ACS disputes it (see C18).

killed.claim: Quintillion's 2025 outage lasted exactly nine months, or exactly seven months.
killed.why: The sources disagree. The applicants say 'seven-plus month' and Broadband Breakfast says 'near nine-month'. No single exact length is supported, so use a hedged range (see C22).

killed.claim: The FCC found that Starlink currently provides wholesale middle mile service in Alaska.
killed.why: The order expressly declines to find this. It acknowledges disagreement and rests on 'regardless of whether' (C18, C19).
